institutionName: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good weather in Athens even during winter, the Greek culture, and to have the experience to live and study in Athens.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great experience. I can only recommend to go to Athens on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Found out most of the things on my own. But, there were some Erasmus student organisations who could help with many things. Regarding the changes in the courses at the university and how the courses would be held, the university did not give very much information. However, it worked well in the end. Just take it easy - so do the Greeks.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I found a facebook page controlled by Erasmus Student Network, so it was easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you do not find an apartment/room too far away from your campus, as Athens is a very big and hilly city, and the public transport is not so reliable. Some days it might be easier to just walk to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It took some time before everything fell into place. But in the end, it worked.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could just text your Erasmus coordinator at the faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I had chosen from home were not offered when I arrived so I made some changes in my learning agreement and chose some other courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just take it easy. It will all manage in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At law school they offered a lot of English courses to Erasmus students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
It was not the most difficult in the world, but still very fine for an Erasmus programme. I did not only go to Greece to study, and there was time to explore Athens, some beatiful Greek islands, some other Greek cities etc. 
So overall, the level was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The professors most of the time just held their lectures by speaking for an hour or two. Some of them asked questions, some did not. 
In the classrooms at the law faculty there were no wi-fi and no opportunity to charge your computer. Therefore, it was sometimes easier just to write notes in hand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Maritime Law 
Intellecutel Property Law
Criminal Procedure and Special Issues in Substantive Criminal Law
International Telecommunications Law
Individual Labour Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I think everyone should choose the courses he/she thinks sound interesting. But I can strongly recommend Maritime Law. The lectures were very interesting and the teacher was very good. 
I can also recommend International Telecommunications Law as the exam in the course was to write a longer essay. It was very flexible that you could just write your essay when you had the time during the semester. 

Join the Greek Laguage Classes even though the University of Copenhagen does not recommend the course. It is nice to learn Greek and to be able to talk with the locals.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food at restaurants was cheaper than in Denmark, so I ate at restaurants often. At the restaurants, buy the local house wine - it is very cheap.
Supermarkets were not that cheap as inflation also had reached Grecce. A bit cheaper than in Denmark, but not much. If you want to buy fruits and greens, then go to the weekly local farmers market in your area - it is cheaper than the supermarket, and everything is completely fresh. 
The public transportation was cheap as you as a student can buy a special student card that lasts for three or six months.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had some sport facilities at the sports department, but I did not use them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to musems, archeological sites etc. Climb some of the hills there are in Athens - The view is amazing. Spend some days just walking around the center of Athens. 
Go out and eat at a local taverna, drink some wine, ouzo, and raki, and have a good time with your new friends - even on a Monday. Just enjoy your life and the spirit of Greece.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Arrange some weekend trips to other parts of Greece.  
Some Erasmus organisations also arrange some trips. 
A part of the experience is to experience Greek culture, and there are plenty of time to do that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go out and drink some coffee or a beer with the people you meet. 
Go to the things arranged by the student organisations in the first weeks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
There can be a lot of demonstrations and strikes in Athens - not only peaceful demonstrations.
The police are massivively present in some parts of Athens - especially in Exarcheia as there are tensions between the state and the locals. You have to get used to that and that you see the police almost everywhere. 
The alphabet is not the latin one - so learn to read Greek.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Greek way of living and enjoying life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not be stressed if something does not go after your first plan. 
Go out and eat at the tavernas and drink coffee at the cafés - Do not spend too much time at home. 
Use the libraries when you want to study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some student restaurants offering free food to the students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience Greek culture and to make some new friendships with people from around all of Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To live in another country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are in doubt if you want to go on an exchange, then just do it. And go to Athens!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
